findings.title: Explicit render in perform_show_response breaks canonical URL on topic pages
findings.body: Adding `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` causes the normal `show` action to render before it executes `canonical_url` (line 87). `canonical_url` sets `@canonical_url` for the layout, so topic show pages will no longer emit the canonical link (or will use a stale one). Move the canonical URL assignment before `perform_show_response`, or render explicitly only from `unsubscribe`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes on missing TopicUser and bypasses TopicUser.change
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil whenever a logged-in user visits the unsubscribe URL without an existing topic_users row (for example a direct visit or a stale email link), and the next `tu.notification_level` call raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Even when the row exists, assigning the level and calling `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not updated and the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is not published, leaving the topic's notification reason stale. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`, which upserts and goes through the normal path.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET without a CSRF/token check
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the current user's notification level in response to a plain GET and is authorized only by the session cookie. A third-party page can therefore embed `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` as an image/link and mute a logged-in user's topic (and email link scanners can trigger it too). Use a signed per-user/per-topic token in the emailed URL, or require a POST with the normal CSRF protection.

findings.title: Unsubscribe route name does not match the added template path
findings.body: The route is declared at top level as `topicUnsubscribe`, so Ember's default template lookup is `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. The PR adds `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path for a nested route named `topic.unsubscribe`, not for a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route. As written the new URL has no template and will render blank or throw a template-not-found error. Either nest the route under the `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` or rename the added template to `topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe only downgrades watching/tracking users to regular
findings.body: When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to regular instead of muted. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so the page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' is false and a mention/reply email can keep arriving after the user clicks the unsubscribe link. Set the level to muted when the intent is to stop notifications, or change the branch and copy to describe a downgrade.

findings.title: No coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The spec change only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options; it does not assert that the rendered body or HTML actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL. There are also no controller/route specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (missing TopicUser, watching/tracking to regular/muted, slug redirect) or for the new Ember route. The nil crash and the notification-level behavior above would pass CI.

findings.title: New locale interpolation makes unsubscribe_url mandatory for all add_unsubscribe_link emails
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` calls this translation from both `body` and `html_part` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, and only UserNotifications was updated to pass the new option. Any other mailer or plugin that uses `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send email. Provide a fallback to `user_preferences_url` or make the option explicitly required and update all callers.
